chunks.content: # The Designer's CLO Journey｜3D Design and Production of Spring/Summer Printed Dresses This document details the step-by-step process of designing and producing spring/summer printed dresses using CLO 3D software, focusing on paperless sample creation, pattern drafting, fabric simulation, and detailed garment finishing. It covers technical terms such as 3D pen tool, pattern alignment, sewing lines, simulation particle diameter, fabric properties, and texture mapping. --- ## Paperless Sample Design Using 3D Pen Tool This section explains how to create a dress design starting without a physical paper sample, using CLO's 3D pen tool for drafting garment pieces directly on the 3D model. - The dress consists of an upper body resembling a neckline top and a lower A-line skirt. - Design begins by drawing the front half of the neckline using the 3D pen tool: - Start at the center front. - Draw lines forming a half-moon cup shape at the bust height. - Use control and shift keys to adjust curve points and maintain line smoothness. - Adjust curves for natural fit by adding or moving curve points. - Draw the back half separately with vertical lines and curves, ensuring alignment and smoothness. - Create princess line patterns on both front and back pieces, adjusting as necessary for smoothness. - Use the flat plate tool to extract the 2D pattern pieces. - Rotate and align pattern pieces along the Y-axis using right-click rotation and alignment functions to ensure consistency. - Perform horizontal symmetry by deleting lines on one side and mirroring the other. - Correct uneven points by deleting curve points or adjusting alignment to achieve straight lines. - Sew front pieces and adjust curves to prevent exaggerated shapes, moving points forward or smoothing corners. - Add shoulder straps approximately 360mm in length to support the garment and prevent slipping during simulation. --- ## Pattern Alignment and Sewing Adjustments This section focuses on aligning pattern pieces precisely and preparing sewing lines for realistic garment simulation. - Align pattern pieces using the back middle line as a reference. - Use the edit board function to fine-tune alignment and symmetry. - Remove unnecessary curve points to straighten edges. - Adjust sewing lines to fold seams to improve fabric drape and evenness. - Use the first key to adjust curves when moving points to avoid sharp edges. - Apply left-right symmetry during sewing to maintain uniformity. - Shoulder straps can be repositioned to prevent sliding; copy and mirror to the other side. - Fix shoulder straps to the model body near the inner edge using the fixing tool to stabilize during simulation. --- ## Lower Body and Layer Construction This section describes the process of creating the skirt portion, including layering, lining, and fabric simulation. - Separate panels for the skirt front and back are created and adjusted for width and length. - Inner lining is constructed slightly smaller than the outer layer, allowing for a slight shrink to prevent visible seams.
